name: Glitchquest
from: Glitch Quest: a retro adventure where the game itself is the antagonist, with misleading instructions and changing universes.
hook: The game is lying to you. Your job is to work out how.
pitch: Three short retro worlds (a Mario-like, a Space Invaders-like, a third of your choice). Signs and hints are sometimes false, by a rule you can learn. Obey a lie and you go back to the checkpoint. The last world tells you to quit; winning means not doing what the game says.
minute_check: Yes, once the first false sign gets you killed.
build_check: Yes with three small worlds; a fixed lying rule keeps it fair.
scope: Three universes. Give the lies a rule (for example, signs in one colour always lie) so testing is a skill, not luck.

brief.player: A hero the player picks, in a world that keeps changing rules.
brief.goal: Get through each universe to the end.
brief.fail: Following an instruction that is a lie (back to the checkpoint).
brief.ending: The final level tells you to quit. Winning means not obeying the game.
brief.verb: Test: try what the game says, and the opposite.
brief.theme: Who to believe when the interface lies. Each universe teaches an expectation and then breaks it.
brief.look: Pixel art that changes style per universe (Mario-like, Space Invaders-like), bright neon.

prov.bug: The sign says this jump is safe!
prov.nit: How does the player learn which signs lie, without just guessing?

refs_lit: An arcade game possessed by its maker; the interface lies and you hack around it.
A narrator who gives instructions you can disobey; the game is about that choice.
Your own reference: a game that remembers what you did and talks back.
omni_gameplay_prompt: Vibrant retro-neon meta-platformer on deep indigo (#140b2b) with bright pixel gold (#ffe86b) and cyan (#3cf2ff) glitching geometry. Steady side-on arcade camera. A small pixel hero approaches a flashing neon arrow sign pointing into a deceptive shimmering floor pit, pauses to test it, leaps backward as the fake floor pixels dissolve into digital static, and hops across hidden solid cyan blocks in the opposite direction while the background warps between 8-bit bricks and starfield vectors. Continuous unbroken gameplay shot, no scene cuts, no gibberish text. Use the reference image for neon glitch style. Sound design: chiptune melody with playful glitch stutters. No dialogue.
